question: Which city was identified as the most polluted in 2023 according to the Sixth Annual World Air Quality Report?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Begusarai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Begusarai has been identified as the most polluted city in 2023 according to the Sixth Annual World Air Quality Report.
 
• The report highlights that Begusarai has the highest concentration of PM2.5 particles in the air, which are harmful to human health.
 
• PM2.5 levels in Begusarai have significantly surpassed the safe limit set by the World Health Organization (WHO).
 
• This alarming level of air pollution is attributed to factors such as industrial emissions, vehicular pollution, and biomass burning.
 
• The findings call for urgent measures to control and reduce air pollution in Begusarai to protect public health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **PM2.5 Particles**

 
 
• PM2.5 refers to particulate matter that is less than 2.5 micrometers in diameter.
 
• These particles can penetrate deeply into the respiratory system and cause health issues such as respiratory infections, heart disease, and lung cancer.
 
 
 
• **World Health Organization (WHO) Air Quality Guidelines**
 
 
• The WHO sets guidelines for air quality to protect public health from the adverse effects of air pollution.
 
• The recommended safe limit for PM2.5 is 10 µg/m³ (annual mean).
 
 
 
• **Sources of Air Pollution**
 
 
• Common sources include industrial emissions, vehicular exhaust, construction activities, and burning of biomass and fossil fuels.
 
• Natural sources such as dust storms and wildfires also contribute to air pollution.
 
 
 
• **Health Effects of Air Pollution**
 
 
• Short-term exposure can cause symptoms like irritation of the eyes, nose, and throat, coughing, and shortness of breath.
 
• Long-term exposure can lead to chronic respiratory diseases, cardiovascular diseases, and increased mortality rates.
 
 
 
• **Measures to Reduce Air Pollution**
 
 
• Implementing stricter emission standards for industries and vehicles.
 
• Promoting the use of public transportation and cleaner fuels.
 
• Increasing green cover through afforestation and urban green spaces.
 
• Raising public awareness about the health impacts of air pollution and encouraging community actions.
